test_plan.strategy: Three-Amigos coverage per FR (happy_path + edge_case + negative), one test case per acceptance criterion so Phase 5 traceability is 1:1. Unit tests drive the pure seams the design introduced for exactly this purpose — Dispatcher.send()'s mute filter and DigestScheduler.Tick(now), which takes the clock as a parameter so no test sleeps or races the wall clock. Integration tests drive real HTTP through the full server handler (auth + CSRF + render). Two e2e cases drive a complete flow end-to-end through the running server (login → page → action → re-render), covering the two critical flows: muting Telegram from Settings, and opening a service's log drawer. Regression is protected by two NFR cases plus the 80 existing test cases, which must keep passing.
test_plan.coverage_goal: 100% of the feature's 25 acceptance criteria have a traced, passing test case; zero regressions in the existing suite.

test_cases.title: No mute window — a fired alert reaches the Telegram notifier
test_cases.given: NotificationMute table is empty; NotificationConfig('telegram') is enabled with bot_token='123:ABC', chat_id='789'
test_cases.when: Dispatcher.send() processes an EventFire for alert{severity:'critical', source:'cpu'}
test_cases.then: the telegram notifier's Notify is invoked exactly 1 time; the email notifier is unaffected
steps: Dispatcher.send() processes an EventFire for alert{severity:'critical', source:'cpu'}

test_cases.title: Open mute window — Telegram is skipped but the alert still persists
test_cases.given: SetNotificationMute(1, now) was called 10 minutes ago (expires_at = now+50m); telegram enabled
test_cases.when: an alert fires and Dispatcher.send() processes it
test_cases.then: telegram Notify is invoked 0 times, AND db.ListAlerts(10) still contains the alert row
steps: an alert fires and Dispatcher.send() processes it

test_cases.title: Expired mute window — delivery resumes with no admin action
test_cases.given: a NotificationMute row with expires_at = now.Add(-1 * time.Second)
test_cases.when: an alert fires and Dispatcher.send() processes it
test_cases.then: telegram Notify is invoked exactly 1 time (the window expired on its own)
steps: an alert fires and Dispatcher.send() processes it

test_cases.title: A 4h mute persists its expiry and survives a reopen of the database
test_cases.given: an empty database at wall time T
test_cases.when: POST /api/notifications/telegram with mute_hours=4 and a valid CSRF token, then the DB handle is closed and reopened
test_cases.then: NotificationMuteUntil() reports muted=true with expires_at within 60s of T+4h
steps: POST /api/notifications/telegram with mute_hours=4 and a valid CSRF token, then the DB handle is closed and reopened
test_cases.expected_result: expires_at - T is within [4h-60s, 4h+60s] and muted == true

test_cases.title: Cancelling an open mute restores Telegram delivery
test_cases.given: an open 24h mute window and an authenticated session
test_cases.when: POST /api/notifications/mute/clear with a valid CSRF token, then an alert fires
test_cases.then: status 200; NotificationMuteUntil() reports muted=false; telegram Notify is invoked 1 time for the next fire
steps: POST /api/notifications/mute/clear with a valid CSRF token, then an alert fires

test_cases.title: An invalid mute duration is rejected and changes no state
test_cases.given: no mute window is open; an authenticated session with a valid CSRF token
test_cases.then: status 400; NotificationMuteUntil() still reports muted=false

test_cases.title: A corrupt mute row fails OPEN — the alert is still delivered
test_cases.given: the NotificationMute row contains an unparseable expires_at value
test_cases.when: an alert fires and Dispatcher.send() processes it
test_cases.then: NotificationMuteUntil() returns muted=false with an error, and telegram Notify is invoked 1 time (never silently swallowed)
steps: an alert fires and Dispatcher.send() processes it

test_cases.title: Full mute flow through the running server: login, mute 4h, section shows remaining time
test_cases.given: a running server with an admin user and a configured Telegram channel
test_cases.when: the client logs in at POST /login, GETs /settings, POSTs mute_hours=4 to /api/notifications/telegram with the page CSRF token, and GETs /settings again
test_cases.then: the re-rendered Telegram section contains 'Muted' and a remaining time of '3h 59m' (or '4h 0m'), and a data-mute-cancel control; no chip-preset mute row is rendered
steps: the client logs in at POST /login, GETs /settings, POSTs mute_hours=4 to /api/notifications/telegram with the page CSRF token, and GETs /settings again

test_cases.title: Digest hour reached — one email lists the last 24h of alerts
test_cases.given: email config {enabled:true, digest_enabled:true, digest_hour:8}; 3 alerts created in the last 24h (critical/cpu, warning/ram, info/network)
test_cases.then: exactly 1 email is sent whose body contains all 3 alerts with their severity, source and timestamp

test_cases.title: At most one digest per calendar day
test_cases.given: email config {digest_enabled:true, digest_hour:8}; DigestState.last_sent_date = '2026-07-13'
test_cases.then: no email is sent

test_cases.title: Zero alerts in 24h still sends one digest saying so
test_cases.given: email config {digest_enabled:true, digest_hour:8}; the Alert table is empty
test_cases.then: exactly 1 email is sent whose body states that no alerts fired (contains 'No alerts')

test_cases.title: Digest disabled — the digest hour passes silently
test_cases.given: email config {enabled:true, digest_enabled:false, digest_hour:8}; 2 alerts in the last 24h
test_cases.then: no email is sent

test_cases.title: The digest never replaces per-event alert emails
test_cases.given: email config {enabled:true, digest_enabled:true, digest_hour:8}
test_cases.when: an alert fires through Dispatcher.send() at 10:00 (not the digest hour)
test_cases.then: the per-event email notifier is invoked exactly 1 time for that fire, independent of digest configuration
steps: an alert fires through Dispatcher.send() at 10:00 (not the digest hour)

test_cases.title: A failing SMTP send is recorded and does not retry-storm
test_cases.given: email config {digest_enabled:true, digest_hour:8}; the email notifier returns an error on every send
test_cases.when: DigestScheduler.Tick(08:00) runs, then Tick(08:01) runs the same day
test_cases.then: exactly 1 send attempt is made in total; an ActionLog row exists with action='digest' and result='failed'; the process does not panic
steps: DigestScheduler.Tick(08:00) runs, then Tick(08:01) runs the same day
test_cases.expected_result: emailSendCount == 1 and ActionLog contains action='digest' result='failed'

test_cases.title: Opening a service's log drawer returns its last 100 journalctl lines
test_cases.given: an authenticated session; a fake privileged helper returning 100 journal lines for source 'service:nginx'
test_cases.then: status 200; the fragment contains the journal lines inside a <pre> block; the helper was called with source='service:nginx' and lines=100
test_cases.expected_result: status 200, body contains the journal content, helper called with ('service:nginx', 100)

test_cases.title: An injection-shaped unit name is rejected before any journalctl runs
test_cases.given: an authenticated session
test_cases.then: status 400 for both; the privileged helper was never called

test_cases.title: Secrets in the journal are redacted and HTML is escaped in the drawer
test_cases.given: a fake helper returning a line containing bot_token=123456:AAHfake and a line containing '<script>alert(1)</script>'
test_cases.then: status 200; the body does NOT contain the raw token '123456:AAHfake'; the body does NOT contain an executable '<script>' tag (it is escaped to <script>)
test_cases.expected_result: body excludes the raw secret and contains '<script>' not '<script>'

test_cases.title: Helper unavailable — the drawer renders an explicit error state, not an empty panel
test_cases.given: an authenticated session; the privileged helper returns ErrUnavailable
test_cases.then: status 200 with a fragment containing 'Could not read logs' (an error state the admin can read), and the fragment is not empty
test_cases.expected_result: status 200 and body contains 'Could not read logs'

test_cases.title: Unauthenticated log-drawer request is redirected to /login with no journal output
test_cases.given: no session cookie
test_cases.then: status 303 with Location: /login; the response body contains no journal content and the helper was never called

test_cases.title: Full drawer flow through the running server: login, /services renders a closed drawer, opening it fetches the tail
test_cases.given: a running server with a mocked systemd runner listing nginx.service and a fake helper returning journal lines
test_cases.when: the client logs in, GETs /services, then GETs the drawer endpoint the row's button declares
test_cases.then: the /services body contains a Logs button with hx-get='/api/services/nginx/logs' and an empty drawer container (no journal content until it is opened); the subsequent drawer GET returns the journal lines
steps: the client logs in, GETs /services, then GETs the drawer endpoint the row's button declares
test_cases.expected_result: services body contains the hx-get logs attribute and no journal content; the drawer GET returns the lines

test_cases.title: Settings renders a hardware section with the four fan modes
test_cases.given: an authenticated session
test_cases.then: status 200; the body contains a hardware section (id='settings-hardware') with data-widget='segmented' data-field='fan_mode' offering exactly data-value='auto','quiet','performance','off'
test_cases.expected_result: body contains settings-hardware and the four fan-mode values

test_cases.title: Saving a fan mode persists it and it renders as selected
test_cases.given: stored HardwareConfig{fan_mode:'auto'}; an authenticated session with a valid CSRF token
test_cases.then: status 200; GetHardwareConfig().FanMode == 'quiet'; the re-rendered page marks the quiet option data-active='true'
test_cases.expected_result: FanMode == 'quiet' and the rendered quiet button carries data-active="true"

test_cases.title: An invalid fan mode is rejected and the stored value is unchanged
test_cases.given: stored HardwareConfig{fan_mode:'quiet'}; an authenticated session with a valid CSRF token
test_cases.then: status 400; GetHardwareConfig().FanMode is still 'quiet'

test_cases.title: A hardware save without a CSRF token is rejected and persists nothing
test_cases.given: stored HardwareConfig{fan_mode:'auto'}; an authenticated session with NO csrf_token field
test_cases.then: status 403; GetHardwareConfig().FanMode is still 'auto'

test_cases.title: Reading the hardware config on a fresh database creates it with defaults and no hardware I/O
test_cases.given: a database with no HardwareConfig row
test_cases.then: it returns FanMode='auto', OLEDEnabled=false, OLEDMetric='cpu' with no error, and the row now exists
test_cases.expected_result: HardwareConfig{auto,false,cpu} and a second call returns the same values

test_cases.title: The hardware section renders the OLED toggle and its four metrics
test_cases.given: an authenticated session
test_cases.then: status 200; the hardware section contains data-widget='toggle' data-field='oled_enabled' and data-widget='segmented' data-field='oled_metric' offering data-value='cpu','ram','temp','ip'
test_cases.expected_result: body contains the oled_enabled toggle and the four oled_metric values

test_cases.title: Saving the OLED configuration persists both the flag and the metric
test_cases.given: stored HardwareConfig{oled_enabled:false, oled_metric:'cpu'}; an authenticated session with a valid CSRF token
test_cases.when: POST /api/settings/hardware with fan_mode=auto, oled_enabled=on, oled_metric=temp, then GET /settings
test_cases.then: status 200; GetHardwareConfig() reports OLEDEnabled=true and OLEDMetric='temp'; the re-rendered page shows the toggle on and temp active
steps: POST /api/settings/hardware with fan_mode=auto, oled_enabled=on, oled_metric=temp, then GET /settings

test_cases.title: An invalid OLED metric is rejected and the stored metric is unchanged
test_cases.given: stored HardwareConfig{oled_metric:'cpu'}; an authenticated session with a valid CSRF token
test_cases.then: status 400; GetHardwareConfig().OLEDMetric is still 'cpu'

test_cases.title: An OLED save without a CSRF token is rejected and persists nothing
test_cases.given: stored HardwareConfig{oled_enabled:false}; an authenticated session with NO csrf_token field
test_cases.then: status 403; GetHardwareConfig().OLEDEnabled is still false

test_cases.title: Omitting the OLED toggle in the POST turns it off (standard HTML checkbox semantics)
test_cases.given: stored HardwareConfig{oled_enabled:true, oled_metric:'ram'}; an authenticated session with a valid CSRF token
test_cases.when: POST /api/settings/hardware with fan_mode=auto and oled_metric=ram, omitting oled_enabled entirely
test_cases.then: status 200; GetHardwareConfig().OLEDEnabled == false and OLEDMetric is still 'ram'
steps: POST /api/settings/hardware with fan_mode=auto and oled_metric=ram, omitting oled_enabled entirely

test_cases.title: The hardware section adds no page-level inline script and keeps the settings controller external
test_cases.given: an authenticated session
test_cases.then: status 200; the body contains <script src="/static/js/settings.js?v= and does NOT contain a page-level inline controller (no "document.getElementById('settings-shell')" in the body)
test_cases.expected_result: settings.js is referenced and no inline controller is present

test_cases.title: The drawer adds no new privileged action: it reuses the helper's existing allow-listed logs action
test_cases.given: a fake helper recording the actions it receives
test_cases.then: the helper receives only the existing 'logs' action with source='service:nginx' and lines=100; no new action name is introduced

test_cases.title: The hardware section joins the existing accordion vocabulary without new client code
test_cases.given: an authenticated session
test_cases.then: the hardware section carries data-settings-section and data-settings-form='hardware' with a data-form-state-host='hardware', exactly like the six existing sections, and every interactive control declares min-h-[44px]
test_cases.expected_result: body contains data-settings-section for settings-hardware, data-settings-form="hardware", data-form-state-host="hardware", and no min-h-[40px] marker

test_cases.title: Adding the hardware section breaks no existing settings form
test_cases.given: an authenticated session with a valid CSRF token and a stored HardwareConfig
test_cases.when: POST /api/performance with sse_interval_sec=5 and POST /api/notifications/telegram with bot_token='123:ABC', chat_id='789' (the pre-existing forms), after the hardware section shipped
test_cases.then: both return status 200 and persist their values; the performance and telegram configs read back unchanged by the hardware feature
test_cases.expected_result: both status 200; GetPerformanceConfig().SSEIntervalSec == 5 and GetNotificationConfig('telegram') still enabled with its token

test_cases.title: Mute activation and cancellation are recorded in action_history
test_cases.given: an authenticated session with a valid CSRF token and no open mute window
test_cases.then: ActionLog contains one row with action='mute' target='telegram' result='success' details containing '4h', and one row with action='mute_clear' target='telegram' result='success'
test_cases.expected_result: two ActionLog rows: action='mute' and action='mute_clear', both result='success'

test_cases.title: An unparseable last_sent_date is treated as never-sent and never blocks the digest
test_cases.given: email config {digest_enabled:true, digest_hour:8} and DigestState.last_sent_date = 'not-a-date'
test_cases.then: exactly 1 email is sent (a corrupt marker never silently suppresses the digest) and last_sent_date is rewritten to '2026-07-13'; the process does not panic

test_cases.title: Prior backups are listed newest first with size, date and an encrypted label
test_cases.given: two ultron-* artefacts on disk, one 48h old and one 1h old
test_cases.then: both filenames appear, the newer one first, with size and creation time, and the .enc artefact is labelled 'encrypted'
test_cases.expected_result: body lists both names; index(newer) < index(older); 'encrypted' label present

test_cases.title: No backups on disk renders an explicit empty state
test_cases.given: an empty backup directory
test_cases.then: 'No backups on disk yet.' is shown and no download link is rendered
test_cases.expected_result: body contains data-backup-empty and no data-backup-download

test_cases.title: Downloading serves the stored encrypted bytes, not a fresh snapshot
test_cases.given: an encrypted backup on disk whose bytes begin with ULTRONENC2
test_cases.then: status 200 and the body is byte-identical to the stored file, begins with ULTRONENC2, and contains no 'SQLite format 3' header
test_cases.expected_result: response bytes == file bytes; ULTRONENC2 prefix; Content-Disposition names the file

test_cases.title: Path traversal and non-artefact names are rejected without serving bytes
test_cases.given: a real backup on disk plus a secret file outside the backup directory
test_cases.when: GET the download route with '../../etc/passwd', an absolute path, and 'not-an-ultron-backup.db'
test_cases.then: none returns 200 and no bytes of the targeted file are served
steps: GET the download route with '../../etc/passwd', an absolute path, and 'not-an-ultron-backup.db'
test_cases.expected_result: status != 200 for each; response never contains the out-of-directory content

test_cases.title: An unauthenticated download returns no file bytes
test_cases.given: an encrypted backup on disk and no session cookie
test_cases.then: status 401 and the body contains none of the stored bytes
test_cases.expected_result: status 401; body excludes ULTRONENC2 and the file content
